mentl/bf04dad:
Root cause: LetDestructure lowers to LBlock([LLet("_dt",...), LLet("n",...)])
which nests inside the evidence closure body as
LBlock([LBlock([bindings...]), LLet(state_update...)]).

collect_free_lowir_list only extends the bound set for LLet nodes at the SAME
level — it doesn't see LLet nodes inside nested LBlocks. So destructured
variable names (n, items) were incorrectly identified as free variables and
captured from the closure's creation scope (frozen initial values) instead of
read from the handler state global (live current values).

Fix: flatten_blocks() unwraps nested LBlocks before building the evidence
closure body. Bindings from destructuring now live at the same level as the
state update, so collect_free_lowir correctly sees them as bound.

Result: The Lux type checker (HM inference, 11-op Infer effect, 6-tuple
handler state, cross-function evidence passing) runs correctly in WASM.
10/10 crucibles pass including wasm_check — check_program("let x = 42")
returns 13 entries on wasmtime.

PLAN.md phases 0 through 5, landed together because they are one change to
what the app is. The notebook kept one sheet and overwrote it; a press keeps
pieces, a desk, and a shelf, and the pieces flow into whatever vessel the
format names.

The state gains pieces, issues, a cycle and an address, and loses todos. An
issue is archived whole on publication, so a back issue reprints as it
shipped rather than as today's draft is configured, and the compile window is
bounded by the last issue's timestamp so issue two cannot reprint issue one.
Photographs held by a shelved issue are pinned against the sweeper, because
sweeping one out from under a published issue would rewrite history.

The imposition is computed rather than eyeballed. PRESET_A and PRESET_B stay
literal and check.sh now holds both equal to the hand kit; everything else is
derived from the page count, which buys A4 and saddle-stitch signatures at
eight, twelve and sixteen pages. Changing format re-flows the same pieces
instead of asking for a retype.

The panel still clips what will not fit, because a printer will too, but it
no longer does so in silence: the fit meter binary-searches the word list and
names the overflow.

The desk is the one deleted in d937b61, rebuilt at n=2. A tray of submitted
pieces, cut-with-restore because a cut is a conversation rather than a
deletion, an editor's note, a bell, and a chair that alternates on issue
parity. Drawing from the log, journal and projects mints pieces rather than
writing panels, so those views are sources now.

An exported issue is the reading view, the imposed sheet, the shelf behind
it, and a working press for the next issue, in one file. It boots from a seed
carried in its own body, hands on a cycle numbered from the issue it holds
rather than the shelf it left, and reaches for nothing on any network. The
